 Zach LaVine tallied 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.
 LaVine returned to the Kings’ lineup on Wednesday after an illness kept him out of Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. While he shot the ball well, the veteran guard’s presence was enough to keep the Kings from finishing their home stand with a seventh straight loss. LaVine has been close to a top-50 player so far, outperforming his ADP. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Keegan Murray and Domantas Sabonis will start Wednesday’s game against the Suns. 
 After missing Sunday’s loss to the Thunder, LaVine and Hunter are back in the Kings’ starting lineup. As a result, Malik Monk and Dylan Cardwell will come off the bench. The other three starters are unchanged. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine (illness) is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Suns. 
 A late scratch for Sunday’s loss to the Thunder, LaVine will be available on Wednesday. His return will push Malik Monk to the bench. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine (illness) is out for Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Absent from the initial injury report, LaVine is now out for Sunday’s game. With De’Andre Hunter questionable and Precious Achiuwa out, the Kings could be extremely shorthanded. Malik Monk and Emanuel Sharp should see their minutes increase with LaVine out. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine recorded 31 points (10-of-16 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic. 
 While fellow Kings veteran Domantas Sabonis went scoreless on Tuesday, LaVine had one of his most productive games of the season. He recorded his second 30-point game of the season, but he had to head to the locker room during the third quarter with an apparent ankle injury. Sacramento doesn’t play again until Friday, so LaVine will have a little time to recover. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine recorded 15 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Heat. 
 LaVine shot the ball well on Sunday, but the playing time was an eye-opener. He played 25 minutes against the Heat and did not return after being subbed out with 4:03 remaining in the third quarter. The Kings made no injury announcement, and LaVine was called for one foul, so foul trouble couldn’t have been the reason. Kings head coach Doug Christie played Darius Acuff Jr. and Malik Monk (9/2/3/1) in the backcourt for the entire fourth quarter, which left no room for LaVine. That’s something for fantasy managers to watch moving forward. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine (elbow) recorded 23 points (8-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Mavericks. 
 After attempting nine shots in Saturday’s blowout loss to the Grizzlies, LaVine got up 14 on Monday. Fantasy managers will be pleased with his efficiency: LaVine shot over 50 percent from the field and made five of nine three-point attempts. With the Kings handing the keys to Darius Acuff Jr., there have been nights when LaVine and Domantas Sabonis (9/7/4/1) don’t get the touches they want. That can be a challenge for fantasy managers, especially if neither LaVine nor Sabonis gets moved before the February trade deadline.

 Zach LaVine (elbow) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 LaVine is dealing with right elbow inflammation. He hasn’t missed a game this season, but if that changes, Malik Monk could take on a bigger role, whether he starts or comes off the bench. 
 Domantas Sabonis 
 SAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #11 
 Domantas Sabonis recorded 11 points (3-of-5 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 14 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Fantasy managers rostering Sabonis received solid returns in rebounds and assists. However, the Kings center took just five shots on Saturday, matching his season low. Sabonis is averaging 9.2 attempts per game, his fewest since 2018-19. Zach LaVine (11 points, one assist) attempted nine shots on Saturday. With rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. having the ultimate “green light,” it will be interesting to see how vets like Sabonis and LaVine adjust. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine recorded 22 points (7-of-10 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 LaVine has scored at least 22 points in each of Sacramento’s first four games, and against the Spurs, he made 70 percent of his shots from the field. With this being a contract year for LaVine, the question is whether a strong first half of the season will put him on the radar of contending teams heading into the February trade deadline. If so, joining a team with meaningful basketball to play in March could preserve LaVine’s fantasy value.

 Franz Wagner accumulated 35 points (13-of-25 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists and one block over 36 minutes to propel the Magic to a 113-111 win over the Nets on Friday.
 Wagner delivered the game-winning bucket on a smooth midrange fadeaway with 2.4 seconds remaining, capping another outstanding performance. He’s continued to thrive with Paolo Banchero sidelined by a high ankle sprain, scoring at least 20 points in seven consecutive games dating back to November 7. He’s topped 30 points five times during that span, rapidly establishing himself as one of fantasy’s most exciting bounce-back performers after injuries limited him to just 34 appearances last season. The Magic have also regained their footing, winning five of their last six games after a brutal 2-9 start. They’ll close out the week with a road matchup against the Wizards on Sunday.
 -  George Bissell

 Julius Randle amassed a team-high 27 points (9-of-20 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists and three steals over 39 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Magic.
 Randle didn’t mince words after Brooklyn was embarrassed by Chicago earlier this week, surrendering 21 three-pointers in the lopsided defeat. He backed up his criticism with his play in this one, finishing one rebound shy of his second double-double of the season while narrowly missing out on his third 30-point performance. He was just 1-of-7 from three-point range, but was pretty efficient otherwise. He’s shaken off a frosty start to the year to deliver early-round fantasy value over the last week, averaging nearly 25 points along with five rebounds, four assists and two steals over his last four games. The Nets have a busy four-game week on tap that includes road matchups against the Timberwolves, Bucks, Raptors and Hornets.
 -  George Bissell

 Nikola Vučević scored a season-high 15 points (5-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds and one assist over 23 minutes off the bench in Friday’s win over the Nets.
 Vučević delivered a perfect shooting performance from the floor, including a trio from beyond the arc, to supply Orlando with double-digit bench points. It wound up being a difference-maker in a close game on the road in Brooklyn. The 36-year-old big man looked pretty cooked by the end of his run in Boston last year and has been a non-factor as a role player during his Orlando return. He remains capable of heating up and knocking down a couple three-pointers off the bench, which the Magic can certainly use.

 Desmond Bane chipped in 21 points (7-of-17 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, five steals and one block over 31 minutes in Friday’s win over the Nets.
 The season-high five thefts were a nice bonus in this one as Bane matched a season-high with seven three-pointers, finishing 7-of-13 from downtown. The sharp-shooting 28-year-old has been outstanding fantasy-wise over the last two weeks, averaging 20 points, 4.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 steals over his last six games. The Magic have won five of their last six and will attempt to keep the momentum going against the downtrodden Wizards on Sunday.

 Josh Giddey had 2 points (1-of-6 FGs), six rebounds, and seven assists in the 98-94 loss to the Wizards on Friday. 
 Giddey had a subpar performance even for his averages this season which are already much lower than expectations. The Bulls closed with Tre Jones over him again. It’s looking really bad for him at this point. It’s hard to drop him at this point, but if you’re in shallower leagues, its hard to find a reason to continue to hold on. His shot attempts are down, his free throw attempts are down, and the percentages are down across the board. They should improve to some degree, but not enough to get close to the value that warranted the spot you drafted him. He could be a buy low in deeper leagues, but giving up anyone that has some level of value could be a mistake. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Nic Claxton got himself 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, an assist, and two blocks in start on Friday against Wizards. 
 In his first start with the Bulls, Claxton had a fine game but nothing crazy to go crazy about. It took Jalen Smith getting hurt for him to get the start. The hopes of him returning to his play in Brooklyn seem to be fading. For his redraft outlook, he’s a streamer for rebounds, but not a lot of upside. Jalen Smith was out with an illness, so it’s possible that he’s back next game.

 Powell took advantage of the Wizards lack of effort on the defensive end. He got going in the first quarter and didn’t look back.
